item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Abiy’s government used emergency powers narrowly and lawfully in a way that clearly constrained abuse. The record is mostly abuse under cover of emergency authority, not lawful restraint.","evidence":[{"title":"Ethiopia: Authorities must stop using state of emergency law to silence peaceful dissent","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-02-19","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/ethiopia-authorities-must-stop-using-state-of-emergency-law-to-silence-peaceful-dissent/","summary":"Amnesty said the state of emergency was being used to silence peaceful dissent through warrantless arrests, curfews, movement limits, and bans on assemblies and associations. This is direct evidence that emergency powers were being used as tools of control rather than narrowly applied public-safety measures.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"Details of State of Emergency Declared by Gov't of Ethiopia","publisher":"ENA English","date":"2024-11-03","url":"https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/en_30124","summary":"The official proclamation centralized coercive authority under an operation command, allowed suspension or replacement of local administrators, restricted CSOs and media suspected of helping “terrorist” groups, imposed ID and movement controls, and suspended judicial authority over enforcement during the emergency. Even though it includes a proportional-force clause, the overall design is broad and coercive, not narrowly tailored.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.1","3B.2","2B.9"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: End the month-long arbitrary detention of thousands in Amhara Region","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-11-06","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/ethiopia-end-the-month-long-arbitrary-detention-of-thousands-in-amhara-region/","summary":"Amnesty reported that federal army and regional security forces rounded up thousands of civilians into makeshift detention camps. This is strong evidence of emergency/security powers being used for mass intimidation and collective punishment.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Ethiopia","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-01-12","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia","summary":"HRW described the Amhara emergency as granting broad warrantless-arrest, curfew, assembly-ban, and search powers, and said security forces repeatedly arrested critics and journalists. That is strong evidence that legal emergency tools were being used to suppress dissent.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"Ethiopia’s Deepening Crackdown on Dissent","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-03-04","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/04/ethiopias-deepening-crackdown-dissent","summary":"HRW reported arrests of opposition figures and journalists under emergency powers, including detention despite judicial processes and repeated arbitrary detention. This points to coercive administrative control rather than lawful, narrow use of security law.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"In Ethiopia, a secret committee orders killings and arrests to crush rebels","publisher":"Reuters via EHRC","date":"2024-02-27","url":"https://ehrc.org/in-ethiopia-a-secret-committee-orders-killings-and-arrests-to-crush-rebels-reuters/","summary":"The EHRC head confirmed a secret security committee that interfered in the justice system and was linked to widespread violations. This is evidence of security governance outside ordinary legal controls, reinforcing the view that coercive measures were not narrowly or lawfully confined.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.1","3B.2","2B.9"]},{"title":"Country policy and information note: actors of protection, Ethiopia, February 2024","publisher":"GOV.UK","date":"2024-01-12","url":"https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ethiopia-country-policy-and-information-notes/country-policy-and-information-note-actors-of-protection-ethiopia-february-2024-accessible","summary":"The note says the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission receives complaints and that some state and federal institutions implemented recommendations on human-rights protections and prison conditions. This is weak positive evidence of complaint handling and oversight capacity, but it does not show emergency powers were used lawfully in 2024.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.1","3B.4"]},{"title":"ICRC Bulletin: Ethiopia, January-June 2024","publisher":"International Committee of the Red Cross","date":"2024-09-13","url":"https://www.icrc.org/en/article/ethiopia-bulletin-january-june-2024","summary":"The ICRC said it maintained dialogue and training on IHL/IHRL for the ENDF, police, militias, and other armed groups. This is a limited positive sign of rule-of-law engagement, but it is training and dialogue, not evidence that emergency or security powers were being used narrowly and lawfully in practice.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.1","3B.4"]},{"title":"Ethiopian Justice Minister Briefs Diplomats about Transitional Justice Policy Implementation","publisher":"ENA English","date":"2024-12-14","url":"https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5626876","summary":"The justice minister said the transitional justice policy aims at accountability, truth-seeking, conditional amnesty, reconciliation, and institutional reform after consultations with civil society and vulnerable groups. This is the best positive institutional evidence, but it is a roadmap and not proof of lawful restraint in the use of emergency or security powers.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.4","3B.1"]}]}
